name: Figure-Four Stretch
summary: Opens the posterior hip with a deep stretch through the glutes and external rotators.
instructions: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh just above the knee. Pull the uncrossed thigh toward your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch through the crossed-leg glute.

name: Seated Figure-Four Stretch
summary: Provides an accessible seated stretch for the glutes and outer hip.
instructions: Sit upright and place one ankle across the opposite thigh. Keeping your back relatively straight, hinge forward until you feel a comfortable stretch in the crossed-leg hip.

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
summary: Opens the front of the hip and can counteract prolonged sitting and repeated hip flexion.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the opposite foot planted in front of you. Tuck your pelvis slightly, squeeze the rear-leg glute, and shift forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the hip.

name: Half-Kneeling Quad Stretch
summary: Creates a strong combined stretch through the quadriceps and front of the hip.
instructions: Begin in a half-kneeling lunge, then bend the rear knee and reach back to hold the rear ankle or foot. Gently pull the heel toward your glute while keeping your torso tall and pelvis controlled.

name: Couch Stretch
summary: Provides an intense quadriceps and front-of-hip stretch by combining knee flexion with hip extension.
instructions: Kneel with one knee near a wall or bench and place that foot behind you against the surface. Bring the opposite foot forward and gradually raise your torso while squeezing the rear-leg glute.

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
summary: Improves hip rotational mobility by placing both hips in opposing 90-degree positions.
instructions: Sit with one leg bent 90 degrees in front and the other bent 90 degrees behind you. Keep your torso tall or hinge over the front leg to deepen the stretch.

name: 90/90 Hip Switches
summary: Actively trains internal and external hip rotation through a controlled range of motion.
instructions: Sit with both knees bent and feet wider than hip width. Rotate both knees from one side to the other under control while keeping your feet planted.

name: Pigeon Stretch
summary: Provides a strong stretch through the glutes and external rotators of the front hip.
instructions: Bring one bent leg in front of your body and extend the opposite leg behind you. Square your hips as comfortably as possible and lower your torso toward the floor.

name: Frog Stretch
summary: Opens the inner thighs and develops hip-abduction mobility.
instructions: Begin on your hands and knees and gradually move your knees wider while keeping your lower legs roughly in line with them. Push your hips backward gently until you feel a stretch through the groin.

name: Butterfly Stretch
summary: Opens the inner thighs and improves comfortable external rotation of the hips.
instructions: Sit tall with the soles of your feet together and allow your knees to fall outward. Bring your feet toward you and gently hinge forward without forcing the knees downward.

name: Adductor Rock-Back
summary: Dynamically opens the groin while allowing controlled movement through hip flexion.
instructions: Start on hands and knees and extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot planted. Slowly push your hips backward, then return forward and repeat.

name: Deep Squat Hold
summary: Develops comfortable mobility in the hips, knees, and ankles at the bottom of a squat.
instructions: Lower into the deepest squat you can comfortably maintain with your feet planted. Keep your chest tall and gently use your elbows against your knees if you want to open the hips further.

name: Standing Forward Fold
summary: Provides a simple bilateral stretch through the back of the legs.
instructions: Stand with your feet around hip width and hinge forward from the hips, allowing your torso to descend toward your legs. Keep a slight knee bend if necessary and relax into the position rather than bouncing.

name: Standing Single-Leg Hamstring Stretch
summary: Isolates one hamstring at a time while allowing precise control of stretch intensity.
instructions: Place one heel slightly in front of you with the leg straight and toes raised. Push your hips backward and hinge forward while maintaining a relatively neutral spine.

name: Seated Single-Leg Hamstring Stretch
summary: Provides a stable floor-based hamstring stretch one leg at a time.
instructions: Extend one leg in front of you and bend the other comfortably. Hinge toward the extended leg from your hips until you feel tension through the back of the thigh.

name: Seated Forward Fold
summary: Stretches both hamstrings simultaneously while encouraging posterior-chain flexibility.
instructions: Sit with both legs extended in front of you. Hinge forward toward your feet while keeping the movement controlled and avoiding aggressive bouncing.

name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
summary: Stretches the hamstrings while keeping the torso fully supported by the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back and raise one leg toward the ceiling. Hold behind the thigh or use a strap around the foot and gradually straighten the knee until you feel a comfortable hamstring stretch.

name: Elevated Hamstring Stretch
summary: Provides an adjustable standing hamstring stretch using an elevated surface.
instructions: Place one heel on a bench or other stable surface with the knee mostly straight. Hinge forward from your hips toward the raised leg without aggressively rounding your back.

name: Sprinter Hamstring Stretch
summary: Combines hamstring lengthening with a position similar to the start of a sprint.
instructions: Begin kneeling with one foot forward, place your hands near the floor, and gradually straighten the front leg while lifting your hips. Return to the lunge position and repeat under control.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
summary: Provides a simple standing stretch through the front of the thigh.
instructions: Stand tall and bend one knee, bringing the heel toward your glute. Hold the ankle and gently pull it closer while keeping your knees relatively close and pelvis controlled.

name: Side-Lying Quad Stretch
summary: Stretches the quadriceps without requiring the balance of a standing variation.
instructions: Lie on your side and bend the top knee. Hold the top ankle and gently draw the heel toward your glute while keeping your hips stacked.

name: Prone Quad Stretch
summary: Provides a supported floor-based quadriceps stretch.
instructions: Lie face down and bend one knee toward your glute. Hold the ankle or use a strap and gently bring the foot closer until you feel a stretch along the front of your thigh.

name: Straight-Knee Calf Stretch
summary: Lengthens the larger superficial calf muscle with the knee extended.
instructions: Place your hands against a wall and step one foot backward. Keep the rear knee straight and heel planted while shifting your body forward.

name: Bent-Knee Calf Stretch
summary: Emphasizes the deeper calf muscles by stretching the calf with the knee bent.
instructions: Take a staggered stance near a wall and keep the rear heel planted. Bend both knees slightly and shift forward until you feel the stretch lower in the rear calf.

name: Downward Dog
summary: Creates a full posterior-chain stretch while also opening the shoulders.
instructions: Start on hands and knees, lift your hips upward and backward, and straighten your arms. Press your chest toward your thighs while gradually working your heels toward the floor.

name: Toe Sit
summary: Opens the bottoms of the feet and improves tolerance to toe extension.
instructions: Kneel with your toes tucked underneath you, then gradually sit your hips back toward your heels. Keep as much weight as comfortable through the toes and back off if the sensation becomes sharp.

name: Shin / Pointed-Toe Sit
summary: Stretches the front of the ankles and lower legs in the opposite direction of a toe sit.
instructions: Kneel with the tops of your feet flat against the floor and gently sit your hips toward your heels. Keep the stretch mild, especially if your ankles are not used to the position.

name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Mobilization
summary: Improves ankle dorsiflexion for squatting, jumping, and other athletic movements.
instructions: Stand facing a wall with one foot flat a short distance away. Drive the knee forward until it gently touches the wall without allowing the heel to lift.

name: World’s Greatest Stretch
summary: Combines hip mobility, posterior-chain lengthening, and thoracic rotation in one full-body movement.
instructions: Step into a deep lunge and place the hand opposite the front foot on the floor. Rotate toward the front leg and reach that arm toward the ceiling, then return and repeat on the other side.

name: Runner’s Lunge
summary: Opens the front of the rear hip in an athletic split stance.
instructions: Step one foot forward into a long lunge and bring your hands toward the floor inside or alongside the front foot. Let the hips sink forward and downward while keeping the rear leg extended or kneeling.

name: Lizard Stretch
summary: Provides a deeper hip-opening variation of a low lunge.
instructions: Begin in a long lunge and bring both hands inside the front foot. Stay on your hands or lower toward your forearms while allowing the hips to settle downward.

name: Cossack Squat Stretch
summary: Dynamically opens the inner thighs while training mobility through a side-to-side squat pattern.
instructions: Take a wide stance and shift your weight toward one leg while bending that knee and keeping the opposite leg straight. Move under control from side to side through the deepest comfortable range.

name: Cat-Cow
summary: Moves the spine through controlled flexion and extension to improve spinal mobility.
instructions: Begin on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Alternate between gently arching your spine and lifting your chest, then rounding your spine and tucking your pelvis.

name: Cobra Stretch
summary: Opens the front of the torso while moving the spine into controlled extension.
instructions: Lie face down with your hands beneath or slightly ahead of your shoulders. Gently press your chest upward while keeping your hips toward the floor and only extending as far as feels comfortable.

name: Sphinx Stretch
summary: Provides a gentler spinal-extension stretch than cobra.
instructions: Lie face down and prop yourself onto your forearms with your elbows underneath your shoulders. Keep your hips relaxed against the floor and gently lengthen your chest forward and upward.

name: Child’s Pose
summary: Provides a relaxed stretch through the back, shoulders, and hips.
instructions: Kneel and sit your hips toward your heels while reaching your arms forward along the floor. Let your chest sink gently downward and relax into the position.

name: Thread the Needle
summary: Improves upper-back rotation while stretching the posterior shoulder.
instructions: Start on hands and knees and slide one arm underneath the opposite arm across the floor. Rotate through the upper back, then return and repeat on the other side.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
summary: Creates gentle rotational mobility through the spine and hips.
instructions: Lie on your back and bring one bent knee across your body toward the floor. Keep both shoulders as close to the floor as comfortable and hold the position without forcing the rotation.

name: Double-Knee Spinal Twist
summary: Provides a gentle bilateral rotational stretch through the lower torso.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and together. Slowly lower both knees toward one side while keeping your shoulders grounded, then repeat on the opposite side.

name: Knees-to-Chest Stretch
summary: Gently flexes the hips and lower spine while providing a relaxed posterior stretch.
instructions: Lie on your back and bring both knees toward your chest. Hold around the thighs or shins and gently draw the legs closer without forcing the position.

name: Kneeling Lat Stretch
summary: Lengthens the lats through an overhead shoulder position while the torso folds downward.
instructions: Kneel in front of a bench and place your hands or elbows on it. Push your hips backward and lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch along the sides of your upper back.

name: Bench Prayer Stretch
summary: Creates a deep overhead stretch through the lats and triceps.
instructions: Kneel in front of a bench with your elbows on the surface and hands together. Sink your chest toward the floor while bending your elbows and allowing your hands to move behind your head.

name: Hanging Lat Stretch
summary: Uses bodyweight to lengthen the lats and overhead shoulder tissues.
instructions: Hold a pull-up bar and allow your body to hang while keeping your feet lightly supported if necessary. Relax into the stretch without forcing your shoulders into an uncomfortable position.

name: Standing Side Lat Stretch
summary: Opens the side of the torso and lengthens the lat through an overhead reach.
instructions: Reach one arm overhead and gently lean your torso toward the opposite side. Keep your chest facing mostly forward rather than rotating excessively.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
summary: Opens the chest and front of the shoulders after pressing or prolonged sitting.
instructions: Place your forearm against a doorway with your elbow bent and step gently forward. Rotate your torso away slightly until you feel a comfortable stretch through the chest.

name: Bilateral Doorway Chest Stretch
summary: Stretches both sides of the chest simultaneously using a doorway for support.
instructions: Place both forearms on opposite sides of a doorway and step forward gradually. Keep your ribs controlled while allowing your chest to move gently through the doorway.

name: Behind-the-Back Chest Stretch
summary: Opens the chest and fronts of the shoulders without requiring equipment.
instructions: Clasp your hands behind your back and gently straighten your arms. Draw your hands slightly backward and downward while lifting your chest.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
summary: Stretches the back of the shoulder through horizontal adduction.
instructions: Bring one arm across your chest and use the opposite arm to gently pull it closer. Keep the stretched shoulder relaxed and avoid rotating your torso.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
summary: Opens the triceps and overhead shoulder position.
instructions: Reach one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head. Use the opposite hand to gently guide the elbow backward and downward.

name: Wall Shoulder Flexion Stretch
summary: Improves overhead shoulder mobility while lengthening the lats.
instructions: Place your hands against a wall or elevated surface and step backward. Push your hips away while lowering your chest between your arms.

name: Sleeper Stretch
summary: Targets internal-rotation mobility at the shoulder.
instructions: Lie on your side with the lower upper arm perpendicular to your torso and elbow bent to 90 degrees. Use the opposite hand to gently rotate the forearm toward the floor without forcing the shoulder.

name: Wall Biceps Stretch
summary: Lengthens the biceps across both the elbow and shoulder joints.
instructions: Place your palm against a wall with your arm straight and slightly behind you. Slowly rotate your torso away until you feel tension through the front of the upper arm.

name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
summary: Opens the palm-side forearm after gripping, lifting, or computer use.
instructions: Extend one arm in front of you with the palm facing upward. Use the opposite hand to gently pull the fingers downward and backward.

name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
summary: Opens the back of the forearm and wrist.
instructions: Extend one arm with the palm facing downward and gently bend the wrist so the fingers point toward the floor. Use the opposite hand to increase the stretch slightly.

name: Prayer Wrist Stretch
summary: Stretches both wrists simultaneously in an easy-to-adjust position.
instructions: Press your palms together in front of your chest with your fingers pointing upward. Slowly lower your hands while keeping the palms together until you feel a stretch through the wrists and forearms.

name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
summary: Relieves tension along the upper shoulder and side of the neck.
instructions: Sit or stand tall and gently tilt one ear toward the same-side shoulder. Keep the opposite shoulder down and use your hand only for light additional pressure.

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
summary: Targets the upper-inner shoulder and back corner of the neck.
instructions: Turn your head roughly 45 degrees to one side and look downward toward your armpit. Gently guide your head farther downward with the same-side hand.

name: Neck Rotation Stretch
summary: Maintains comfortable rotational mobility of the neck.
instructions: Sit or stand tall and slowly turn your head toward one side as far as comfortably possible. Return to center and repeat on the opposite side without forcing the range.

name: Standing Side Bend
summary: Opens the side of the torso through lateral spinal flexion.
instructions: Stand tall and reach one arm overhead. Lean gently toward the opposite side while keeping both feet planted and your chest mostly forward.

name: Full-Body Reach
summary: Provides a simple whole-body lengthening movement suitable for waking up or resetting after sitting.
instructions: Stand tall and reach both arms overhead while lengthening through your torso. Rise slightly through your feet if comfortable, then lower and repeat smoothly.
